$comment: Read by `yarn i18n:translate` and by anyone translating by hand. `untranslated` terms stay exactly as written (case may follow the language's rules where noted). `fixed` terms always use the given translation. `style` is per-locale guidance.

untranslated.Electron Fiddle: Product name. Never translate or shorten.
untranslated.fiddle: A small Electron project that this app edits and runs. Keep the English word. German: "Fiddle" (neuter, das Fiddle, plural Fiddles). Japanese: "Fiddle".
untranslated.gist: A GitHub Gist. Keep the English word. German: "Gist" (der Gist, plural Gists). Japanese: "Gist".
untranslated.Electron Forge: Product name. "Forge" on its own also stays.
untranslated.API names and code: Code identifiers (BrowserWindow, ipcMain, app.whenReady(), process.versions), file names (main.js, preload.js, renderer.js, index.html, package.json), command-line flags, environment variables, URLs and keyboard shortcuts stay exactly as written.
untranslated.Placeholders: {{name}} placeholders and $t(...) references stay exactly as written, including their names. They may move within the sentence.

Make (Forge command).ja: インストーラーを作成

Preload script.ja: プリロードスクリプト

Stable / Beta / Nightly (release channel.ja: 安定版 / ベータ版 / ナイトリー
Stable / Beta / Nightly (release channel.zh-CN: 稳定版 / Beta 版 / Nightly 版

Keyboard shortcut.ja: キーボードショートカット

style.*: Sentence case where the language has case. Keep the ellipsis character (…) on labels that open a dialog. Keep it short: buttons and menu items must fit their maxLength. Don't add trailing punctuation to labels, buttons or menu items.
style.de: Informal "du", as in GitHub's German UI. Use imperatives for buttons and menu items ("Speichern", "Datei öffnen …"). Put a space before the ellipsis ("Öffnen …"). Use German quotation marks („…“).
style.ja: Polite です／ます form for sentences; noun or verb phrases without です for buttons, menu items and titles. Full-width punctuation (、。「」). No 。 at the end of labels or buttons. Put a space between Latin words and Japanese text only where it aids readability (e.g. "Electron のバージョン").
style.zh-CN: Simplified Chinese (mainland) following Visual Studio Code and Microsoft terminology (撤消, 帐户, 快捷方式, 包 for packages, 修订 for gist revisions, 机密 for secret gists). Formal 您 only where a pronoun is unavoidable; otherwise omit it. Full-width punctuation (，。：？！（）) and curly quotes “”; no trailing punctuation on labels, buttons or titles, 。 at the end of full sentences. Put a space between Chinese and Latin words or numbers ("Electron 版本", "运行 fiddle"), but not next to full-width punctuation. Keep the ellipsis … on labels that open a dialog.
style.zh-TW: Traditional Chinese as used in Taiwan, following Visual Studio Code and Microsoft Taiwan terminology (檔案, 資料夾, 設定, 預設, 套件, 處理序, 指令碼, 索引標籤). Avoid second-person pronouns where possible and use 您 when needed; full-width punctuation (，。：；！？「」（）), no full stop on labels, buttons or titles; a half-width space between Latin words or numbers and Chinese text; fiddle and gist stay lowercase Latin.
style.pt-BR: Brazilian Portuguese, neutral você register: infinitive for buttons, menu items and labels ("Salvar", "Abrir…"), polite imperative for instructions to the reader ("Escolha", "Verifique"). Sentence case, ellipsis … with no space before it, curly quotes “…”, decimal comma and thousands dot. Use VS Code/Windows terms: arquivo, pasta, guia (tab), excluir, padrão, tela, Configurações; "versão" for release; "o fiddle" and "o gist" are masculine (plural fiddles, gists).
style.es: Neutral international Spanish: informal tú (no vosotros, no voseo) in sentences, impersonal infinitives for buttons and menu items, VS Code terminology (Configuración, Agregar, Eliminar, Borrar, Alternar, Paleta de comandos), third-person present for CLI help. Sentence case, ¿…? and ¡…! pairs, ellipsis … with no space before it, non-breaking space before %, curly quotes “…”. Avoid Spain-only or Latin-America-only words: equipo (not ordenador/computadora), archivo (not fichero), portapapeles. Short labels Main, Preload and Renderer (sidebar sections, console filters, file names) stay in English; fiddle and gist are masculine (el fiddle, los gists); build local for a local Electron build.
style.ru: Formal "вы" (polite imperatives such as «Введите», «Проверьте») or impersonal wording, never "ты"; terminology follows Visual Studio Code's Russian UI (Параметры, Правка, Вид, Справка, Палитра команд). Sentence case, «…» quotation marks, ellipsis … with no space before it, ё written out, non-breaking space before an em dash and between a number and % or МБ. Keep fiddle and gist in Latin script as indeclinable words and phrase around them so no gender agreement is needed; plural forms one/few/many/other.
style.ko: Polite formal register (합니다체) as in Visual Studio Code and Windows: sentences end in ~합니다/~하세요/~하시겠습니까?, buttons and menu items are noun or verb-stem forms without a final period (실행, 파일 열기…), status titles are short nouns (다운로드 완료). Keep Fiddle, Gist, GitHub, npm and Electron in Latin script and choose the particle by their Korean pronunciation (Fiddle을/이, Gist를/가, GitHub을, Electron을); around placeholders reword to avoid particles instead of writing 을(를). Use “ ” quotes as in the source and the ellipsis character (…) with no space before it.
style.fr: Formal "vous" or impersonal infinitives/imperatives, as in Visual Studio Code and Windows French (buttons: infinitive or noun, e.g. "Enregistrer", "Ouvrir…"). Sentence case; non-breaking space (U+00A0) before : ; ? ! % and inside « »; typographic apostrophe ’; ellipsis … with no space before it; "fiddle", "gist", "package" and "build" are masculine and stay in lowercase English; "jeton" for token, "étendue" for scope, "correcte/défectueuse" for good/bad in bisect.
style.tr: Buttons and menu items use the bare imperative ("Kaydet"); sentences addressed to the user use the polite "siz" imperative ("girin", "seçin"); errors use the impersonal passive ("… açılamadı"). Suffixes on foreign words take an apostrophe and follow pronunciation (fiddle'ı, gist'i, npm'de, GitHub'da), suffixes are never attached to {{placeholders}}, and "%" precedes the number ("%50").
